summary: Read an integer and write how many of its bits are equal to 1. Bits equal to 0 add nothing to the count. That count is the Hamming weight of the bit pattern. If the language offers only signed integers, count the bits of the given pattern anyway, and do not first turn a negative value into its absolute value. An input shown as -3 under two's complement still contributes every 1 in that pattern. The usual width is 32 bits, and high zeros do not raise the count.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is tokens in the same order as the method parameters.
